answer: Use `SB_OIDC_CA_FILE`, pointing it at a PEM certificate for your private CA. Certificate verification stays enabled.

Memory for: My OIDC provider uses a certificate from a private CA. Which environment variable points SilverBullet at it?
[1] Single Sign-On.md (Single Sign-On)
  - A private certificate authority can be supplied to SilverBullet with SB_OIDC_CA_FILE, pointing to a PEM certificate trusted for provider connections; certificate verification remains enabled.
  OpenID Connect providers: The server must reach the issuer’s discovery, authorization metadata, token and key endpoints. A private certificate authority can be supplied with `SB_OIDC_CA_FILE`, pointing to a PEM certificate trusted for provider connections. Certificate verification remains enabled.
  OpenID Connect providers: Create a confidential OIDC client, register the displayed callback and enable Authorization Code with PKCE. Use the provider’s issuer URL and client credentials. The provider must supply a stable subject and a verified email, using the `openid`, `email` and `profile` scopes. / SilverBullet’s provider integration tests use [Pocket ID](https://pocket-id.org/docs/), but the same generic configuration is intended for standards-compliant providers such as [Authentik](https://docs.goauthentik.io/add-secure-apps/providers/oauth2/), [Authelia](https://www.authelia.com/integration/openid-connect/introduction/), [Keycloak](https://www.keycloak.org/securing-apps/oidc-layers), and [ZITADEL](https://zitadel.com/docs/guides/integrate/login/oidc). Provider defaults vary, so verify the required scopes, PKCE support, client authentication method, and `email_verified` claim with the sign-in test before enabling SSO. ID tokens with additional audiences (such as a ZITADEL project ID) are accepted when their `azp` claim equals the client ID. The user’s email must be verified at the provider.

  - The callback URL displayed by SilverBullet must be copied into the provider's client configuration, and its path is /.auth/central/oidc/callback.

Exact facts:
- [1] SilverBullet (in multi-space mode) supports SSO via OpenID Connect (OIDC). Administrators provision accounts individually and assign them to spaces. Local username/password accounts remain available alongside SSO accounts.
- [1] 4. Copy the displayed callback URL into the provider’s client configuration. The path is `/.auth/central/oidc/callback`. Each space does not need a separate provider callback.
